analysis.title: 2027 Bitcoin Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions
key_insights: Bitwise forecasts bitcoin at $1.6 million by 2036, a 34.3% 10-year CAGR, and calls it the best-performing major institutional asset over the decade. Last year's forecast was 28.3% CAGR to $1.3 million by 2035.

Bitcoin fell 53% from its October 2025 high to its June 2026 low. Bitwise says this fits its long-term return expectations and is much shallower than prior cyclical drawdowns, which averaged more than 80%.
The thesis rests on three factors: growing institutional adoption and net inflows, rising demand for hard-asset exposure as a hedge against inflation and debasement, and limited, inelastic supply.

Institutional investors control about $147 trillion (per BCG). Bitwise expects them to allocate 1% to 5% to bitcoin, which implies $1.5 trillion to $7.4 trillion of purchases against roughly $14 billion of new bitcoin issued per year.

US spot bitcoin ETPs hold $108 billion in assets less than three years after launch. Bitwise expects flows to accelerate in 2027 and beyond, helped by approvals on several large wealth management platforms in 2026.
About 20.1 million of 21 million bitcoin (95.7%) are in circulation. Annual issuance inflation is 0.8%, falling to 0.4% in 2028 and 0.2% in 2032, versus about 2% for gold.

US federal debt is $40.2 trillion, double its level a decade ago. Debt is 121% of GDP, interest payments are $1.1 trillion a year, and would approach $1.5 trillion if the debt were refinanced at prevailing rates.

The US ran a $2.0 trillion deficit in fiscal 2026, $218 billion more than the prior year and $140 billion above the CBO's February projection. Outlays hit a record $7.4 trillion and the deficit was 6.2% of GDP. DOGE claimed $215 billion of cuts, about 10% of its $2 trillion target.

G10 10-year yields rose year over year in every country listed, with the US at 5.28% (+113 bps), the UK at 5.42% (+73 bps), France at 4.86% (+132 bps) and Japan at 3.07% (+142 bps). Bitwise reads this as a sign debt dynamics may be near a tipping point.
Since 2020 bitcoin returned 1,069% (43.95% CAGR), the best of the major assets, ahead of gold at 174% and US equities at 162%.
Dollar share of global FX reserves fell to 56.7% from 71.0% in 1999. Central bank gold purchases reached a record $96 billion in 2025, up 14% on 2024 and 4.4x the level of a decade ago.

Sovereign bitcoin adoption is slowly progressing. The Czech National Bank bought a $1 million test portfolio in November 2025, Luxembourg's sovereign wealth fund put 1% into bitcoin ETFs in October 2025, and Deutsche Bank research argues bitcoin and gold will sit on central bank balance sheets by 2030.

The Clarity Act, a major US crypto bill, failed to advance in Congress in 2026 over ethics provisions. Bitwise flags this as a future regulatory risk but still sees the regulatory trend as positive overall.

Valuation uses a total addressable market model. The base case assumes bitcoin captures 25% of the store-of-value market ($109.8T by 2036), 1% of institutional assets, 1% of emerging market currencies, 5% of offshore wealth and 2.5% each of national treasuries, corporate treasuries and remittances. Bear case is $130,686 (4.6% CAGR), bull case is $3,667,911 (46.0% CAGR), from a $83,557 starting price.

Bitcoin's 10-year average correlation is low across assets: 0.25 to US equities, 0.02 to bonds, 0.11 to gold. Its 90-day correlation to gold hit a record 0.58 on September 11, 2026. Its 90-day correlation to equities has never exceeded 0.75.

Bitwise forecasts 10-year correlations to bitcoin of 0.43 for US equities, 0.05 for bonds, 0.21 for gold, 0.39 for private equity and 0.30 for private credit. It overweights recent correlation trends in this forecast.
Modeled volatility is 27.8% for the full 10 years, the midpoint between current and expected 2036 levels. The model assumes volatility declines at half the historical rate.

Bitcoin peaked at $126,080 on October 6, 2025 and fell to $58,717 on June 30, 2026 (-53.4%). If that low holds, it is the shallowest cyclical retracement on record versus prior declines of 86%, 84% and 77%. Bitwise's base case is that the four-year cycle weakens but does not disappear.

In Bitwise's comparison with JPMorgan, PGIM, BlackRock and Vanguard capital market assumptions, bitcoin has the highest return (34.3%) and volatility (27.8%). Private equity is next at 10.8%, US equities 6.7%, gold 5.5% and US bonds 5.0%.

Key risks are bitcoin's limited track record, regulatory and legislative change, uncertain continued institutional adoption, and technical risk including quantum computing or AI-driven mathematical advances that could break bitcoin's cryptography.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Debt has doubled in a decade, which Bitwise cites as support for hard-asset demand.
High debt load raises the odds of currency debasement, supporting store-of-value assets.
A deficit this large during strong growth signals structural fiscal strain.
Third-largest budget line item. It would rise close to $1.5 trillion if the debt were refinanced at prevailing rates.
Markets are demanding higher yields to finance growing debt.

macro_indicators.indicator: US dollar share of global FX reserves
macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 71.0% in 1999, indicating weaker dollar dominance.
A record, up 14% on 2024 and 4.4x a decade ago.
Bitwise base case, above last year's 28.3%.

crypto_views: Base case bitcoin price of $1,599,766 by 2036 (34.3% CAGR); bear case $130,686 and bull case $3,667,911.
US spot bitcoin ETPs hold $108 billion in assets and Bitwise expects inflows to accelerate in 2027 and beyond.
Nearly 96% of all bitcoin that will ever exist is already owned, mostly by retail investors, while most institutions hold 0%.
Institutions are expected to allocate 1% to 5% of portfolios to bitcoin, meaning $1.5 trillion to $7.4 trillion of purchases.
Bitcoin's 90-day correlation to gold reached a record 0.58 on September 11, 2026, and Bitwise expects the relationship to deepen.
More than a dozen countries, including the US, hold bitcoin reserves. The Czech National Bank and Luxembourg's sovereign wealth fund added exposure in the past year.
The Clarity Act failed to advance in Congress in 2026, which Bitwise flags as an opening for future regulatory risk.
Nearly every major US financial institution has launched a crypto initiative, including BlackRock, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley.
risk_factors: Limited track record: bitcoin has traded widely only since 2010, and spot ETPs launched in 2024.
Regulatory and legislative risk, including the failure of the Clarity Act and no certainty the current positive environment will persist.
Institutional, corporate and government adoption are new trends and may not persist.
Technical and quantum risk: quantum computing or AI-accelerated mathematics could threaten bitcoin's cryptography, and a major upgrade to quantum-resistant cryptography will likely be needed.
Bitcoin remains a cyclical asset subject to significant drawdowns.
Forecasts that rely on historical data may not hold if future macro conditions differ.
charts_described: US federal debt rose from $19.6T in September 2016 to $40.2T in September 2026.
US Treasury outlays hit $7.4T in FY2026, $386B more than FY2025.
Annual central bank gold purchases reached $96B in 2025, up 4.4x over the decade.
US dollar share of global FX reserves fell from 71.0% in 1999 to 56.7%.

Bitcoin cycle chart shows returns of 410,507%, 11,107% and 2,020% in prior cycle up-phases, with drawdowns of 86%, 84% and 77%, and 696% followed by a 53% drawdown this cycle. Cycle lengths were 4.04, 3.92 and 3.94 years, with 3.86 years so far.
vol_and_positioning: Bitcoin's volatility and its volatility of volatility have declined for a decade. Bitwise models 27.8% annualized volatility over the next 10 years.
The model assumes the rate of volatility decline will be 50% slower than the historical trend.
The 53% drawdown from the October 2025 peak to the June 2026 low compares with prior cyclical declines of 86%, 84% and 77%.
Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with US equities has rarely exceeded 0.50 and never exceeded 0.75.
Bitcoin's average correlation to bonds is about 0.00, mostly within a -0.25 to 0.25 band.
cross_bank_references: Deutsche Bank published research arguing bitcoin and gold are the future of central bank reserves and will likely sit on central bank balance sheets by 2030.
Alliance Bernstein projects bitcoin above $1.0 million by 2033 and Standard Chartered projects above $0.5 million by 2030, which Bitwise says aligns with its forecast.
ARK Invest's bull case is roughly $1.2 million by 2030 and Strategy's Michael Saylor projects $21.0 million by 2046, both more aggressive than Bitwise.

tension_points.bull_case: Institutional demand of $1.5T to $7.4T meets inelastic supply of about $14B a year. Fiscal debasement pressure pushes investors toward hard assets, and a 53% drawdown shallower than the 77-86% of past cycles shows maturing support.
tension_points.bear_case: Bitcoin has a limited track record and remains a cyclical asset subject to significant drawdowns. Regulatory setbacks such as the failed Clarity Act, uncertain continued institutional adoption, and quantum or AI-driven cryptographic risk could undermine the forecast.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the June 30, 2026 low of $58,717 fails, the shallowest-retracement argument no longer holds. Bitwise also names a failure of institutional adoption to persist and a major quantum or mathematical breakthrough against bitcoin's cryptography.

theme_stances.key_argument: Institutional allocations of 1% to 5% meeting limited, inelastic supply should drive bitcoin to $1.6 million by 2036.
theme_stances.evidence: bitcoin will be the best-performing major institutional asset over the next decade

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising sovereign debt and interest burdens push governments toward currency debasement, raising demand for gold and bitcoin.
theme_stances.evidence: it pays to bet on that happening
